providers.title: The average gap
providers.scope: (1/N) sum_(n<=N) (p_(n+1) - p_n)/log p_n -> 1, by the prime number theorem.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: At most a proportion 1/C of large gaps
providers.scope: For every C > 0, the upper density of the n with p_(n+1) - p_n > C log p_n is at most 1/C.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: A positive proportion of large gaps
providers.scope: For every C > 0 there are c(C) > 0 and N_0(C) with #{n <= N : p_(n+1) - p_n > C log p_n} >= c(C) N for all N >= N_0(C) (OpenAI, 2026).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Increases of p_n/n
providers.scope: The set of n with p_n/n < p_(n+1)/(n+1) has positive lower density (question of Erdős and Prachar).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: From adjacent intervals to gaps
providers.scope: If for at least delta X integers m in (X, 2X] the interval (m, m+h] contains a prime and (m+h, m+2h] none, then at least delta X/h distinct primes in (X, 2X+h] are followed by a gap longer than h.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: A prime coordinate of a divisor sum
providers.scope: If m + b_j is a prime with log(m+b_j)/log X larger than the budget, the smooth divisor sum equals the sum of one dimension less with the last argument of the test function set to 0.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Bombieri-Vinogradov with moving endpoints
providers.scope: For fixed sigma < 1/2, K >= 1, A > 0: sum_(q <= X^sigma) mu^2(q) K^omega(q) E_X(q) << X (log X)^(-A), where E_X(q) is the maximal error for primes in reduced classes in (X+a, 2X+a] with |a| <= D (log X)^B.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Density sums
providers.scope: The average over X < m <= 2X of a product of smooth divisor sums, optionally times theta(m+a_0), equals an explicit finite density sum up to O((log X)^(-A)), uniformly in shifts of size at most a power of log X; total budget below 1, or below 1/2 with the prime factor.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Convergence of the singular series
providers.scope: The singular series of a finite set converges absolutely, is nonnegative, vanishes exactly when the set meets every class modulo some prime, and equals 1 for a single point.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Singular series of pairs
providers.scope: S({0, delta}) = 0 for odd delta and 2 C_2 prod_(p | delta, p > 2) (p-1)/(p-2) for even delta, C_2 the twin-prime constant.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Mean one modulo small primes
providers.scope: The singular series truncated at y has average exactly 1 over all tuples of residues modulo the product of the primes up to y.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Gallagher's average in boxes
providers.scope: For s fixed and intervals I_1, ..., I_s of length h inside an interval of length K h, the sum of the singular series over distinct tuples with a_i in I_i is h^s (1 + O(1/log log h)).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Correlations of smooth divisor sums
providers.scope: Average of a product of smooth divisor sums, optionally times one shifted prime: L^(-t) (S(H) C + O(L^(-1/2) (log L)^A)), t the number of distinct divisor shifts, S the singular series, C an integral of complete mixed derivatives when every shift occurs at most twice.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Fourier representation of test functions
providers.scope: A smooth compactly supported function is an absolutely convergent Fourier integral of exponentials exp(-sum (1 + i u_l) v_l), with the same representation for its complete mixed derivative.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Euler products and the singular series
providers.scope: The non-zeta part of the Euler product of a density sum equals the singular series up to O(L^(-1/2) (log L)^A), uniformly in frequencies up to sqrt(L); valid when the singular series vanishes.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Zeta near 1
providers.scope: For Re z > 0 and |z| <= 1, |zeta(1+z) - 1/z| <= 3.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Cumulative test functions
providers.scope: The cumulative integral of f in C_c^infty of the simplex {sum t_i < 1/8} is a test function whose signed complete mixed derivative is f; deleting a coordinate at 0 corresponds to f_j + T f_(j+1).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Moments of the square
providers.scope: For Z = sum over subsets S of the second block of D_(F_|S|)(m; S): E Z^2 -> w, E Z^4 = O(1), E Z^2 V_J -> lambda w, E Z^2 V_I -> v = lambda sum alpha_j ||f_j + T f_(j+1)||^2, and limsup E Z^2 V_J^2 <= (lambda + lambda^2 c_G^2) w.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Deletion at a prime of the second block
providers.scope: If m + a is prime with a in the second block, Z(m) is the same signed sum over subsets of the block without a, with F_j replaced by F_j + F_(j+1)(., 0).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: A profile spread over many scales
providers.scope: For lambda, beta > 0 there is g >= 0 in C_c^infty((0, infinity)) with int g^2 = 1, int g = sqrt(lambda) and int u g^2 < beta.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The cancelling family
providers.scope: Alternating product functions on the r = floor(sqrt k) top levels give 1 - s^2/(k d^2) <= w <= 1 and v/lambda <= 2/r + (r/k)^2 + 4 s^2/(k d^2).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Large gaps: the complete statement
providers.scope: For every C > 0 a positive lower density of n satisfy p_(n+1) - p_n > C log p_n, and the increases of p_n/n have positive lower density (OpenAI, 2026).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review
